rows.rationale: Semiquinone is an on-path FAD redox intermediate; the mechanism ends in hydride transfer from FAD hydroquinone to NADP+, fitting the v1 flavin dehydrogenase/reductase fingerprint.

Mixed heme-Cu terminal oxidase/proton-pumping chemistry is broader than the seed examples, but heme-mediated O2 reduction remains close enough that OOS relabel is not fail-closed. Exact blocker: need a heme_copper_terminal_oxidase subfamily policy before separating it from heme_peroxidase_oxidase.

BA3 cytochrome-c oxidase has heme/Cu binuclear terminal oxidase chemistry. It should be reviewed with m_csa:714 if a heme_copper_terminal_oxidase future family is opened; current evidence is not strong enough for OOS relabel.

Curated text explicitly describes FAD semiquinone radical and Fe-S coordinated radical dehydration rather than ordinary v1 flavin hydride-transfer dehydrogenase/reductase chemistry. Canonical revision artifact closes this row.
Fe-S appears as downstream sulfur-transfer/biogenesis context; the catalytic mechanism is PLP internal/external aldimine and enzyme-persulfide chemistry, fitting the PLP seed.
Semiquinone is part of the FAD redox cycle following NADH hydride transfer and single-electron transfer to cytochrome b5; this is in-scope flavin reductase chemistry.
Mechanism text explicitly supports hydride transfer to flavin N5 and states there is no evidence for a radical; heuristic radical match is a false positive.

summary.broader_scan_recommendation: No automatic broad relabels. The observed strong canonical mismatch rate is low; use targeted future-family review for heme-copper oxidases and radical flavin/Fe-S chemistry instead of a full 210-row manual scan now.
